classification.difficultyReason: Systematically distinguishes eight configurations by parallelism and concurrence. Geometry language is the closest listed skill; configuration enumeration has no exact catalogue match.

content.prompt: There are eight possible ways to place four distinct lines in a plane. Five of these configurations involve parallel lines; the other three do not. Draw all eight of them.

answer.short: The eight configurations are shown below: four parallel lines; three parallel lines and a transversal; two pairs of parallel lines; exactly one parallel pair with the other two lines meeting off both parallel lines; exactly one parallel pair with three lines concurrent; four concurrent lines; exactly three concurrent lines with no parallel pair; and no parallel pair or three concurrent lines.
answer.worked:
Classify first by parallel lines, then by concurrence.

With parallel lines there are five cases: all four parallel; three parallel and a fourth crossing them; two parallel pairs; one parallel pair with the other two lines meeting away from both parallel lines; and one parallel pair with the other two lines meeting on one of the parallel lines.

With no parallel lines there are three cases: all four concurrent; exactly three concurrent; and no three concurrent. The drawings illustrate these incidence relationships; rotations and changes of spacing do not create additional cases.

spec.description: Eight complete solution figures arranged in four rows of two. Matching single or double arrow marks identify parallel families. Ordinary geometry is black under house style.
spec.mathematics: Cases 1–5 contain parallel lines: parallel-family sizes 4, 3+1, 2+2, and 2+1+1 with either no triple concurrence or one triple concurrence. Cases 6–8 have no parallel pair and respectively four concurrent lines, exactly three concurrent lines, or no triple concurrence.
